walk.note: approved v017 speeds; stair_factor slows walking on the Stair 1 ramps; step_ft = largest surface height change accepted per sub-step

level1.encoding: per row: run lengths, alternating open / blocked, starting with open
level1.rule: open = inside the Level 1 face-of-stud outline and no base-building or tenant solid between 0.5 ft and 6.5 ft; Stair 1 run 1 cells are a ramp surface

level1_lobby_A.encoding: per row: run lengths, alternating open / blocked, starting with open
level1_lobby_A.rule: as level1 plus the Lobby Concept A solids (banquettes, directory, wood boxes) as blockers; used while the lobby concept is shown

level2.encoding: per row: run lengths, alternating open / blocked, starting with open
level2.rule: open = under an upward face of the approved Level 2 slab (16 ft 0 in) and no base-building, tenant or lobby-concept solid between 16.5 ft and 22.5 ft; Stair 1 run 1, landing and run 2 cells are the navigation surface; voids have no floor; no openings were added

stair_surfaces.source: 12 treads INT_Stair1_run2_tread_* (v014, frozen); Level 2 at 16.0 ft

stair_surfaces_note: Viewer-only navigation surfaces (invisible; not in the Blender master; not rendered). A ramp's height at distance d along the run is z_base + riser_ft * (0.5 + d / tread_ft), clamped to z_max. Guards, walls and the Level 2 void edge stop the walker through the grids and the step_ft rule.
